message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I would be the asshole if I asked my daughter to find a different hobby. Let me start by understanding the situation. My daughter, Ann, is 17 and has been obsessed with building miniatures since she saw the movie Hereditary a few months back. She's spent almost $500 on miniatures from various places, all using her own money from her part-time job at a movie theater. I can't cut her off financially because it's her money, but I'm really annoyed by this hobby. I think it's driving me crazy, maybe because the movie was creepy, or maybe because I want to spend quality time with her instead of her being in her room all the time. I've tried suggesting other activities, like going for a walk or joining cheerleading, but she always says no. My husband thinks it's sweet and even lets her display her miniatures around the house and in his office. Every day, I'm surrounded by these miniatures, and I realize I haven't had a real conversation with her that doesn't revolve around glue types. Her grades are okay (Bs), she does her chores, but her spare time is entirely consumed by this hobby. I know I might be the asshole, but would I be the asshole if I asked her to find another hobby that could help her in life, something she could put on a resume? Hmm, so I need to consider a few things here. First, is her hobby harmful? She's using her own money, her grades are fine, she's responsible with chores. So, in terms of negative impact, it doesn't seem like it's causing any harm. It's just that I'm feeling disconnected from her because of this. I also need to think about her interests. She's finally found something she's good at, and it's a creative outlet. Maybe I'm projecting my own feelings onto her. I want her to have hobbies that I approve of, but that might not be fair to her. On the other hand, I'm concerned about her future. I want her to have skills or experiences that can help her in life, maybe something more traditional or resume-worthy. But is that a valid concern? Or is it more about my own insecurities about her not engaging in activities I value? I should also consider how she feels about this. She's invested a lot of time and money into her hobby. If I push her to change, it might make her feel unappreciated or misunderstood. It could damage our relationship. Maybe instead of asking her to find a different hobby, I could encourage her to explore other interests alongside her current hobby. That way, she can still enjoy what she loves while also developing other skills or experiences. I also need to reflect on why this is bothering me so much. Is it because I'm worried about her social life or future, or is it because I'm feeling neglected? If it's the latter, maybe I should find ways to spend quality time with her that don't revolve around her hobby, but still respect her interests. In the end, I think it's important to support her passions, even if they're not what I would choose. Encouraging a balanced life where she can pursue her interests while also engaging in other activities might be a better approach than trying to force her to change her hobby.
